## Data Analysis

### 1 Read Data
Only data from those who participated in the vignette experiment was used.

```{r}
data_t2 <- read.csv(here("01_data/b_sab_mzp2_2024_data_file.csv")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(vig == 1 | vig == 2 | vig == 3)
```

### 2 Measures

#### 2.1 Confirmatory  Factor Analysis (CFA): Social Support Scales  
Items measuring social supports were developed aligning with Richter at al. [-@richter2011], Schulz and Schwarzer [-@BSSS], and our theoretical understanding of social support. We adapted the perspective to that of the educators (social support providers). Five items were created for each dimension of social support. The factorial structure of three dimensions was tested calculating a confirmatory factor analysis. 

Data for CFA:

```{r}
data_cfa_1 <- data_t2 %>%
  dplyr::select(sozunt_ins5:sozunt_ins2)
```

Describe data:

```{r}
data_cfa_1_sorted <- data_cfa_1[, sort(colnames(data_cfa_1))]
describe(data_cfa_1_sorted)
```

*Step 1: Fitting a Three-factor Model*

```{r}
# specify the model
cfa_model_ss <- ' inf =~ sozunt_inf1 + sozunt_inf2 + sozunt_inf3 + sozunt_inf4 + 
                         sozunt_inf5
                  emo =~ sozunt_emo1 + sozunt_emo2 + sozunt_emo3 + sozunt_emo4 + 
                         sozunt_emo5
                  ins =~ sozunt_ins1 + sozunt_ins2 + sozunt_ins3 + sozunt_ins4 + 
                         sozunt_ins5 '

# fit the model
fit_cfa_ss <- lavaan::cfa(cfa_model_ss, 
                          data = data_cfa_1,
                          ordered = TRUE,
                          estimator = "DWLS",
                          test = "scaled.shifted",
                          missing = "pairwise")

# evaluate the model
summary(fit_cfa_ss, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)
```

Model fit was poor:

```{r}
# CFI cut-off: > .95; SRMR cut-off: < .08; RMSEA cut-off: < .06
lavaan::fitmeasures(fit_cfa_ss, c("cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled", "srmr"))
```

Since factor loadings of on the instrumental support factor `ins` were low for several  items, we operationalized instrumental support based on the three highest-loading items `sozunt_ins1`, `sozunt_ins2`, `sozunt_ins3`, which are closely aligned with the theoretical notion of providing material, and reran the CFA. Subsequently, `sozunt_emo1` was also discarded because of the low factor loading. The subsequent model is as follows:

```{r}
# specify the model
cfa_model_ss_2 <- ' inf =~ sozunt_inf1 + sozunt_inf2 + sozunt_inf3 + sozunt_inf4 + 
                           sozunt_inf5
                    emo =~ sozunt_emo2 + sozunt_emo3 + sozunt_emo4 + 
                           sozunt_emo5
                    ins =~ sozunt_ins1 + sozunt_ins2 + sozunt_ins3 '

# fit the model
fit_cfa_ss_2 <- lavaan::cfa(cfa_model_ss_2, 
                            data = data_cfa_1,
                            ordered = TRUE,
                            estimator = "DWLS",
                            test = "scaled.shifted",
                            missing = "pairwise")

# evaluate the model
summary(fit_cfa_ss_2, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)
```

Model fit was acceptable:

```{r}
# CFI cut-off: > .95; SRMR cut-off: < .08; RMSEA cut-off: < .06
lavaan::fitmeasures(fit_cfa_ss_2, c("cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled", "srmr", "cfi.robust", "rmsea.robust"))
```

*Step 2: Evaluating Reliability (omega)*

```{r}
compRelSEM(fit_cfa_ss_2)
```

*Step 3: Interpretation of factors*  

We proceeded with the following model:

- Factor 1: Informational support (“Tips and advice”) was best represented through the items `sozunt_inf1`, `sozunt_inf2`, `sozunt_inf3`, `sozunt_inf4` and `sozunt_inf5`.

- Factor 2: Emotional support ("Comfort and nearness") was best represented through the items `sozunt_emo2`, `sozunt_emo3`, `sozunt_emo4` and `sozunt_emo5`.

- Factor 3: Instrumental support ("Provision of goods and materials") was best represented through the items `sozunt_ins1`, `sozunt_ins2` and `sozunt_ins3`. 


#### 2.2 Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA):  Self-Efficacy Scale
Tickell and Klassen [-@tickell2024] developed a  scale for measuring teacher mentoring self-efficacy beliefs and suggest a two-factor model, with factors named as *Pedagogical Practices* and *Professional Relationships*. We tested this factor structure in our German translation of the questionnaire:

Data for CFA:

```{r}
data_cfa_2 <- data_t2 %>%
  dplyr::select(seffsab_1:seffsab_9)
```

Describe data:

```{r}
describe(data_cfa_2)
```

*Step 1: Fitting a Two-factor Model*

```{r}
# specify the model
cfa_model_se <- ' pae =~ seffsab_1 + seffsab_2 + seffsab_20 + seffsab_14 + 
                         seffsab_6 + seffsab_28 + seffsab_48 + seffsab_39 +
                         seffsab_46 + seffsab_47 + seffsab_4
                  rel =~ seffsab_29 + seffsab_44 + seffsab_27 + seffsab_43 + 
                         seffsab_9 '

# fit the model
fit_cfa_se <- lavaan::cfa(cfa_model_se, 
                          data = data_cfa_2,
                          ordered = TRUE,
                          estimator = "DWLS",
                          test = "scaled.shifted",
                          missing = "pairwise")

# evaluate the model
summary(fit_cfa_se, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)
```

Model fit was poor:

```{r}
# CFI cut-off: > .95; SRMR cut-off: < .08; RMSEA cut-off: < .06
lavaan::fitMeasures(fit_cfa_se, c("cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled", "srmr"))
```

Evaluating modification indices:

```{r}
inspect_fit_cfa_se <- lavaan::modindices(fit_cfa_se, sort = TRUE, minimum.value = 10)

inspect_fit_cfa_se
```

- `seffsab_48` was removed (justified by similarity of content with `seffsab_39`, which in contrast covered the construct better) 

We reran the CFA:

```{r}
# specify the model
cfa_model_se_2 <- ' pae =~ seffsab_1 + seffsab_2 + seffsab_20 + seffsab_14 + 
                           seffsab_6 + seffsab_28 + seffsab_39 +
                           seffsab_46 + seffsab_47 + seffsab_4
                    rel =~ seffsab_29 + seffsab_44 + seffsab_27 + seffsab_43 + 
                           seffsab_9 '

# fit the model
fit_cfa_se_2 <- lavaan::cfa(cfa_model_se_2, 
                            data = data_cfa_2,
                            ordered = TRUE,
                            estimator = "DWLS",
                            test = "scaled.shifted",
                            missing = "pairwise")

# evaluate the model
summary(fit_cfa_se_2, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)
```

Model fit was still not as good as desired:

```{r}
# CFI cut-off: > .95; SRMR cut-off: < .08; RMSEA cut-off: < .06
fitMeasures(fit_cfa_se_2, c("cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled", "srmr"))
```

Evaluating modification indices again:

```{r}
inspect_fit_cfa_se_2 <- lavaan::modindices(fit_cfa_se_2, sort = TRUE, minimum.value = 10)

inspect_fit_cfa_se_2
```
- `seffsab_2` was removed (justified by similarity of content with `seffsab_1`, which in contrast covered the construct better) 
- `seffsab_27` was removed (justified by ambiguity with regard to both factors) 

We reran the CFA:

```{r}
# specify the model
cfa_model_se_3 <- ' pae =~ seffsab_1 + seffsab_20 + seffsab_14 + 
                           seffsab_6 + seffsab_28 + seffsab_39 +
                           seffsab_46 + seffsab_47 + seffsab_4
                    rel =~ seffsab_29 + seffsab_44 + seffsab_43 + 
                           seffsab_9 '

# fit the model
fit_cfa_se_3 <- lavaan::cfa(cfa_model_se_3, 
                            data = data_cfa_2,
                            ordered = TRUE,
                            estimator = "DWLS",
                            test = "scaled.shifted",
                            missing = "pairwise")

# evaluate the model
summary(fit_cfa_se_3, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)
```

Model fit improved:

```{r}
# CFI cut-off: > .95; SRMR cut-off: < .08; RMSEA cut-off: < .06
fitMeasures(fit_cfa_se_3, c("cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled", "srmr"))
```

*Step 2: Evaluating Reliability (Omega)*

Both scales showed acceptable reliability:

```{r}
compRelSEM(fit_cfa_se_3)
```
*Step 3: Contrasting a One-factor Model*

```{r}
# specify the model
cfa_model_se_4 <- ' sef =~ seffsab_1 + seffsab_20 + seffsab_14 + 
                           seffsab_6 + seffsab_28 + seffsab_39 +
                           seffsab_46 + seffsab_47 + seffsab_4 +
                           seffsab_29 + seffsab_44 + seffsab_43 + 
                           seffsab_9 '

# fit the model
fit_cfa_se_4 <- lavaan::cfa(cfa_model_se_4, 
                            data = data_cfa_2,
                            ordered = TRUE,
                            estimator = "DWLS",
                            test = "scaled.shifted",
                            missing = "pairwise")
```

Model fit:

```{r}
# CFI cut-off: .95; SRMR cut-off: .09
fitMeasures(fit_cfa_se_4, c("cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled", "srmr"))
```

Compare to two-factor-model:

```{r}
anova(fit_cfa_se_3, fit_cfa_se_4)
```

The Two-factor Model describes the data better.


#### 2.3 Compute Scale Scores

Unfold code to see scale construction:

```{r}
data <- data_t2

## Vignette as factor
data$vig <- as.factor(data$vig)

## Attribution 

data <- data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(int = int_1,  # Internality
                sta = sta_1,  # Stability 
                con = kon_1)  # Controllability

## Social Support

# Informational support
data <- data %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(inf_sup = rowMeans(subset(data, select = c(sozunt_inf1,
                                                           sozunt_inf2,
                                                           sozunt_inf3,
                                                           sozunt_inf4, 
                                                           sozunt_inf5)),
                                   na.rm = TRUE),

# Emotional support
                emo_sup = rowMeans(subset(data, select = c(sozunt_emo2, 
                                                           sozunt_emo3, 
                                                           sozunt_emo4,
                                                           sozunt_emo5)),
                                   na.rm = TRUE),
# Instrumental Support
                ins_sup = rowMeans(subset(data, select = c(sozunt_ins1, 
                                                           sozunt_ins2, 
                                                           sozunt_ins3)),
                                   na.rm = TRUE))

## Self-efficacy

# Pedagogical Practices   
data <- data %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(sef_pea = rowMeans(subset(data, select = c(seffsab_1, seffsab_20, 
                                                           seffsab_14, seffsab_6, 
                                                           seffsab_28, seffsab_39,
                                                           seffsab_46, seffsab_47, 
                                                           seffsab_4)),
                                   na.rm = TRUE),

# Relationships
                sef_rel = rowMeans(subset(data, select = c(seffsab_29, seffsab_44, 
                                                           seffsab_43, seffsab_9)),
                                   na.rm = TRUE))

```


#### 2.4 Glossary

*Attributions*   
adapted from [@steinsmeier1985]

- `int`: Internality
- `sta`: Stability
- `con`: Controllability

*Social Support*  
adapted from [@richter2011]

- `inf_sup`: Informational support
- `emo_sup`: Emotional support
- `ins_sup`: Instrumental support

*Self-efficacy*  
adapted from [@tickell2024]

- `sef_pea`: Pedagogical Practices
- `sef_rel`: Relationships

#### 3.3 Path Analysis

Independent variables were mean centered and standardized, before the interaction terms were calculated:

```{r}
data <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(int, con, sta, inf_sup, emo_sup, ins_sup, sef_pea, sef_rel, vig) 

# mean center and standardize independent variables
data$int_cntrd <- scale(data$int, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
data$sta_cntrd <- scale(data$sta, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
data$con_cntrd <- scale(data$con, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)

# Interaction terms
data$conXint <- data$con_cntrd * data$int_cntrd 
data$intXsta <- data$int_cntrd * data$sta_cntrd 
```

##### 3.3.1 Controlability

```{r}
model <- '
  inf_sup ~ int_cntrd + con_cntrd + conXint
  emo_sup ~ int_cntrd + con_cntrd + conXint
  ins_sup ~ int_cntrd + con_cntrd + conXint
  
  inf_sup ~~ emo_sup
  emo_sup ~~ ins_sup
  inf_sup ~~ ins_sup
  
  int_cntrd ~~ con_cntrd
  con_cntrd ~~ conXint
  int_cntrd ~~ conXint
'

fit_ses <- lavaan::sem(model = model, 
                       data = data, 
                       missing = "FIML",
                       estimator = "ML",
                       meanstructure = TRUE,
                       se = "bootstrap", 
                       bootstrap = 1000)

parameterEstimates(
  fit_ses,
  standardized = TRUE,
  rsquare = TRUE,
  ci = TRUE,
  level = 0.90
)
```

Model fit:
```{r}
fitMeasures(fit_ses, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "srmr", "rmsea"))
```

##### 3.3.2 Internality

```{r}
model <- '
  inf_sup ~ int_cntrd + sta_cntrd + intXsta
  emo_sup ~ int_cntrd + sta_cntrd + intXsta
  ins_sup ~ int_cntrd + sta_cntrd + intXsta
  
  inf_sup ~~ emo_sup
  emo_sup ~~ ins_sup
  inf_sup ~~ ins_sup
  
  int_cntrd ~~ sta_cntrd
  sta_cntrd ~~ intXsta
  int_cntrd ~~ intXsta
'

fit_ses <- lavaan::sem(model = model,
```

##### 3.3.4 Constructivist and Transmissive Mentoring

```{r}
model <- '
  inf_sup ~ con_men + tra_men
  emo_sup ~ con_men + tra_men
  ins_sup ~ con_men + tra_men
  
  inf_sup ~~ emo_sup
  emo_sup ~~ ins_sup
  inf_sup ~~ ins_sup
  
  sef_rel ~~ tra_men
'

fit_ses <- lavaan::sem(model = model, 
                       data = data_t1t2, 
                       missing = "FIML",
                       estimator = "ML",
                       meanstructure = TRUE,
                       se = "bootstrap", 
                       bootstrap = 1000)

parameterEstimates(

)
```

#### 3.3 Descriptives: Vignettes

*Were the situations cause equally attributed?*

```{r}
data_vig1 <- data_t2 %>% 
  dplyr::filter(vig == 1) 

data_vig2 <- data_t2 %>% 
  dplyr::filter(vig == 2) 

data_vig3 <- data_t2 %>% 
  dplyr::filter(vig == 3) 

tab4 <- data.frame(int = mean(data_vig1$int_1, na.rm = TRUE),
                   sta = mean(data_vig1$sta_1, na.rm = TRUE),
                   con = mean(data_vig1$kon_1, na.rm = TRUE))

tab5 <- data.frame(int = mean(data_vig2$int_1, na.rm = TRUE),
                   sta = mean(data_vig2$sta_1, na.rm = TRUE),
                   con = mean(data_vig2$kon_1, na.rm = TRUE))

tab6 <- data.frame(int = mean(data_vig3$int_1, na.rm = TRUE),
                   sta = mean(data_vig3$sta_1, na.rm = TRUE),
                   con = mean(data_vig3$kon_1, na.rm = TRUE))

barplot(as.matrix(tab4), main = "Vignette 1")
barplot(as.matrix(tab5), main = "Vignette 2")
barplot(as.matrix(tab6), main = "Vignette 3")
```

*What reasons were given for the situation?*
